title: A Sacrifice of Thanksgiving
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: The God who owns the cattle on a thousand hills doesn't need our offerings or our good works. He wants wholehearted worship, and it becomes a loop of delight.
exhortation: The question I want to ask is this: what pleases the Lord? Does God need sacrifices, blood and money? It might seem so: endless animal sacrifices, tithes, everything you earn. Obviously God requires these things because he wants them. Wrong. The captain-obvious question is: why would the God who owns the cattle on a thousand hills need you to give him cattle he already owns?

Imagine offering animal sacrifices every day, thinking that's all it's about, and then being confronted with this. Imagine the puzzled look on the Israelites' faces as it dawned on them: why does the God who owns everything need all this?

But are we any different? Don't we often come to God waving the sacrifice of our good, tidy lives, our moral behavior, our time and wealth, maybe even good causes: giving to the poor, building churches, disaster relief or a thousand other things we hang our hat on, thinking, "Surely God must be happy with me now"? The answer is another resounding no. He doesn't find pleasure in our good works, wealth and reputation on their own.

So what does he actually want from us? Verse 14: "Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and perform your vows to the Most High, and call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me." He wants your wholehearted worship. Not the worship of a slave, but of a chosen, redeemed child who has seen the worth, beauty and majesty of God and delights to reflect his goodness back to him in praise.

These verses introduce us to God's intention for all humanity: an endless worship loop. Step one: offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving and praise his name. Step two: perform your vows, obeying his commands and delighting in his word, as Psalm 119 says. Step three: put your trust in the Lord and call on him. Step four: God intervenes and delivers you. Step five: once you're delivered, you glorify him, which is step one again. Like a flywheel that gathers speed as it spins, the praise of God is meant to build and grow until it consumes you. He doesn't want your money or your skills. He wants your wholehearted devotion, because like a good father he wants what is best for his children, and he knows that delighting in him will be our greatest delight.
prayer: Lord, it is so much better when it's all about you. When you are the focus of our gratitude, our praise and our purpose, everything falls into place. Forgive us for straying and for thinking we know a better way. What we need is to lift our eyes to you, follow hard after you and worship you with a whole heart.

Give that gift today to those watching. Plant a seed of gratitude in their hearts, a seed of praise for who you are and what you've done: your grace toward us, your provision, generosity, faithfulness and patience. There is so much to look to. Lift our eyes off our troubles and fix them on you, Jesus. In your precious name, amen.
